why: UNIVERSES: theorem_18_1_12_one/two/three/three_reflexive at universe 0; the eleven witnesses have none. (2), (3) and the reflexive (3) match: A states them for a given covering family c, B with ∃ c in the hypothesis of (3) and without c in (2); when no covering family exists, IsReflexiveAuxNormFunctor holds vacuously and N₁ = 0, N₂ = ⊤ do it. The two statements differ in (1): A's theorem_18_1_12_one assumes F̄(α) ≠ ∅ for every α (HasStrongBundleUniformizers) and concludes Definition 18.1.7 in the direct form (IsAuxNormDirect), while B's (1) has no hypothesis and concludes the model reading IsAuxNormFunctor. B ⇒ A's (1) goes through the reference covering family and Lemma 18.1.8 (IsAuxNormIn.isAuxNormDirect). A's (1) does not give B's (1) when no F̄(α) is assumed nonempty, so in A_to_B B's (1) is proved directly: from any covering family, Theorem 12.2.2 in its model pushed forward (the argument of exists_isAuxNormFunctor), and vacuously when there is none; that clause does not use A. The witnesses in B_to_A are re-proved with their own proofs, the item's theorems replaced by B's clauses.
